title: The standard deduction
subject: Money

text: This is the amount the IRS lets you subtract before tax is figured.
For most working people it is larger than anything they could itemize.
Single or married filing separately: $15,750. Married filing jointly: $31,500. Head of household: $23,625.
Age 65 or blind adds more. There is also a temporary extra senior deduction for 2025 through 2028, with income limits.
Itemizing means listing mortgage interest, state taxes, charity, and medical expenses above a floor.
If that list is smaller than the standard deduction, take the standard deduction. Most wage earners do.
It is one or the other. Software will compare them. Married filing separately: if your spouse itemizes, you generally must too.
A renter with no big medical bills almost always takes the standard deduction.
You are single. Your itemized deductions add up to $4,200. Which do you take?

choices.label: The $15,750 standard deduction. It is larger.
Itemize. Listing things always saves more.

text: Take the larger of the standard deduction or your itemized list. Most workers take the standard.

notes: Example course. Tax year 2025 figures, filed in 2026. Confirm on IRS.gov. Not tax advice.
